parsed.why: Strong local protections—public-accommodation bias law, protected bathroom access, hate-crime recourse, care shield—lift it above the national 0.35, but border/document exposure and unresolved ballot pressure keep it Elevated, not safe.

Most-protective tier: public-accommodations enforcement, X IDs, care shield, hate-crime recourse and low recorded trans-homicide rate; national passport/entry and custody exposures still cap it below Reduced.

Shield law, long-standing bias and hate-crime protections, open state IDs and care coverage raise it; documented birth-sex prison placement and no housing rule are local custody exposure, leaving it slightly below the best.

Sanctuary, nondiscrimination, facilities rulings and ID access are strong, but recent trans murders and unresolved custody placement, plus universal national border exposure, hold it just below the top protective states.

Worst-laws tier: school/public facility ban, no gender-identity bias or hate-crime protection, religious refusal, hostile name-change ruling and dual-listed birth certificates add local exposure on top of the severe national border regime.
